engineNotes.v2.4: Measured on the v2.4 engine: nine opponent archetypes, a four-rung ladder in which every rung starts from the hundred the rung below it finished at, and two objectives rather than one. Tuned and Max maximize win rate. Pod Fun is scored against a 30-45% win-rate band with the ceiling enforced as a constraint, weights the pod-experience metric at 20%, and is floored at 75% of its own Tuned build's power so it can never come out the stronger deck.

engineBoundaryNote: Every build in this file was measured on v2.4, so the rungs are comparable with each other. They are not comparable with figures published before it: the win-rate band alone moves a dominant deck's score by ten points or more, and that is a change of question rather than a change of answer.

caveats.note: The six decks My actually plays were measured on a different brief from the other forty-four. Their Pod Fun rung was searched over his own bench at zero spend, with the win rate held under 60% rather than under this file's 45% ceiling — his instruction, and the reason all six are listed above as over the ceiling. It is also why five of them out-power their own Tuned rung: a search that may spend nothing but may reorder a hundred cards is free to find a better hundred, and on these lists it did.

1o.honestRead: Holds up. Teneb is a genuine reanimator, which is what this shell already wants, and it measures a hair above Betor (+0.2 — inside noise). Betor's end-step lifegain-to-counters engine is invisible to the model, so the true gap likely favors Betor. Swap only if you prefer the play pattern, not for the number.

3e.honestRead: Real gain, real cost. Hazel measures +4.5 over Gitrog, but the optimizer's response to her is to strip TEN lands from a 48-land lands-matter deck — she pays off tokens, not landfall. That is not a minor tweak; it converts the Golgari Land Engine into a different deck. Adopt only if you want that rebuild.

5o.altCommander: Kirol, History Buff // Pack a Punch
5o.honestRead: Kirol, History Buff // Pack a Punch measures 1.22 points above Quintorius, Loremaster on this exact hundred, which is larger than the 0.14 the seed-to-seed noise would explain. Read it narrowly: the field is only the 6 legends already inside this deck whose color identity covers every card in it, the ninety-nine is identical in both runs, and the engine scores a commander on what it does in combat and on the board — a body it can swing is worth more to it than a trigger it cannot model.

1a.honestRead: Modest gap, essentially within noise. Slimefoot's sacrifice-and-drain loop and Lathril's go-wide Elf engine both lean on effects (death triggers, token-swarm mana sinks) the model only partially credits, so treat +0.1 as a coin flip rather than a real edge -- keep Slimefoot.

1b.honestRead: No alternative already in this deck beats Betor, Ancestor's Voice by more than the seed-to-seed noise (-6.68 against 0.24), so the commander in the box is the right one on this evidence. The field is only the 1 legend already inside the deck whose color identity covers every card in it, not every legal commander in the colors.

1c.altCommander: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
1c.honestRead: Real gap, but Liesa's own text is more invisible to the model than Vito's. The command-zone life tax and the 'whenever a player casts a spell, lose 2 life' drain are both outside anything the engine pattern-matches, so her true score sits higher than 70.7 -- Vito's lifegain-doubling is comparatively simple and well-credited. Treat the +15.0 gap with real skepticism.

1e.honestRead: Real gap. Ghave's counters-into-Saprolings-into-counters loop converts through tokens, and tokens are modeled as extra power on the creature that makes them rather than a separate, resilient board -- that undersells Ghave's actual wipe-resilience. Rishkar's one-shot ETB counters on up to two creatures is simpler and fully visible, which is most of why it measures ahead. Treat the gap as real but somewhat overstated.

2o.honestRead: Large gap, but The Reaper's whole identity -- -1/-1 counters and stealing opponents' creatures when they die with one -- sits entirely outside the model (counters only track +1/+1 growth; there is no steal-on-death pattern). Mazirek's sacrifice-triggered +1/+1 counter engine is squarely inside the modeled counter growth, so it measures fairly. The real gap is smaller than 17.8, but Mazirek is a genuine, well-supported upgrade for a Jund sacrifice/counters shell either way.

2a.honestRead: Xanathar's stax-flavoured upkeep lock (opponent can't cast, you may play their top card) has no matching pattern in the classifier at all -- it reads as a vanilla body. Grimgrin's self-counters-and-removal loop is squarely inside the model's growth and removal patterns. Treat +10.3 as overstated; Xanathar's real disruption value is simply invisible here.

2b.honestRead: Sheoldred's graveyard-recursion-plus-symmetric-drain kit is mostly legible (reanimation, drain), and Kalitas's repeatable removal-into-a-token measures only +3.1 above it -- inside the range where either is a reasonable pick. No strong recommendation either way.

2e.honestRead: Oloro already ranks first of sixteen on its own lifegain-into-cards loop. No alternative measured beats it.

3o.honestRead: No alternative already in this deck beats Purphoros, God of the Forge by more than the seed-to-seed noise (-6.75 against 0.19), so the commander in the box is the right one on this evidence. The field is only the 1 legend already inside the deck whose color identity covers every card in it, not every legal commander in the colors.

3c.honestRead: Aesi's extra-land-drop-into-a-card-per-landfall is simple, repeatable draw the model credits correctly, so this is a real comparison. Rishkar's ETB counters-and-mana-ability engine still measures well ahead -- a genuine, well-supported upgrade, though it trades a card-advantage plan for a counters-and-ramp one, not a free upgrade to the same deck.

3d.altCommander: Dion, Bahamut's Dominant // Bahamut, Warden of Light
3d.honestRead: Large gap, but Sythis's simple enchantment-cast lifegain-and-draw is the more transparent of the two: Dion, Bahamut's Dominant transforms into a Saga whose mass +1/+1 counters and removal chapter are exactly the kind of text this model reads well, while the model likely can't apply 'each other creature' correctly to every creature on a wide board (it has no real multi-target counter grant, only a one-shot-to-the-biggest-creature approximation) -- so even 81.1 probably understates the real Bahamut. Three of fifteen candidates also failed to resolve here (double-faced names). Treat this as a real, if imprecisely measured, gap.

3f.honestRead: Omnath's landfall payoff is a 5/5 token every land drop, and tokens are modeled as extra power on the creature that makes them rather than separate, hard-to-wipe-around bodies -- that undersells exactly what makes a wide landfall board resilient. Its death-trigger damage is also outside anything the classifier reads. Bristly Bill's counters-and-doubling engine is fully visible to the model. Treat +11.9 as a real but overstated gap.

4o.altCommander: Dion, Bahamut's Dominant // Bahamut, Warden of Light
4o.honestRead: Real gap. Kangee's flying-team pump is simple and already well-credited; Dion, Bahamut's Dominant adds a token, a keyword, and an eventual removal-and-counters transformation, all of which register cleanly. This one holds up as a plausible upgrade.

4a.honestRead: Only three candidates matched Brago's narrow identity and theme combination, so this reads on a thinner field than most other cases. Brago's blink-for-value loop (exile and return your own permanents on combat damage) has no ETB-value pattern in the classifier, while Jason Bright's sacrifice-into-a-counter-and-flying is squarely inside the modeled counter growth. Treat +10.3 as understating Brago, whose whole plan of re-triggering enter-the-battlefield effects is invisible here.

4b.honestRead: The largest gap measured, and the least trustworthy. Shorikai's real plan -- crew 8 to become a copy of a huge exiled artifact or creature -- has no equivalent in this model; its {1},{T} loot ability is the only part that registers, so 57.1 reflects almost none of the deck's actual game plan. Black Panther's damage-reflection and mana-sink counters read as simple, well-credited combat value. Do not treat 25.4 points as a real measurement of the gap between these two commanders.

4e.honestRead: Roon of the Hidden Realm measures 0.29 points above Chulane, Teller of Tales on this exact hundred, which is larger than the 0.15 the seed-to-seed noise would explain. Read it narrowly: the field is only the 2 legends already inside this deck whose color identity covers every card in it, the ninety-nine is identical in both runs, and the engine scores a commander on what it does in combat and on the board — a body it can swing is worth more to it than a trigger it cannot model.

5c.honestRead: Syr Gwyn's draw-on-attack is tied to 'equipped creature attacks,' a condition the classifier doesn't parse, so only partial credit for the draw shows up. Alexios's repeatable +1/+1 counter growth lands directly on himself, a creature, which is squarely inside the modeled counter growth and scores accordingly. Real gap, but adopting Alexios trades the equipment-tribal shell for a different combat plan entirely.

5d.honestRead: Aurelia's extra combat phase is one of the strongest effects in the format -- functionally two attack steps a turn -- and there is no 'additional combat' pattern in the classifier, so none of that value is scored; only her keywords (flying, vigilance, haste) register. Black Panther's counters-and-pump kit is comparatively simple and fully visible. Treat +13.9 as a significant understatement of Aurelia, not a real case for swapping.

5e.honestRead: Modest real gap. Trostani's populate-into-lifegain is simple and well-credited; Rosie Cotton's token-triggered counters engine measures a genuine but not dramatic edge. Reasonable either way.

5f.honestRead: Aryel already ranks first of sixteen on its Knight-tribal removal engine. No alternative measured beats it.

6o.honestRead: Muldrotha already ranks first of sixteen on its graveyard-replay engine, essentially tied with Titania (-0.2, inside noise). No case for swapping.

6c.honestRead: Small gap, close to noise. Nethroi's mutate-reanimation and Teshar's historic-spell reanimation are comparably legible to the model; no strong recommendation either way.

6d.honestRead: Kruphix already ranks first of sixteen. Its devotion-gated creature status is invisible to the model (devotion isn't tracked), so it's scored as an enchantment the whole game -- which, if anything, understates the risk real opponents' removal poses to it, not its value. No alternative measured beats its unlimited-hand-size and colorless-mana-saving text.

6e.honestRead: Old Stickfingers already ranks first of sixteen on its self-mill-into-reanimation-targets plan. No alternative measured beats it, and the gap to Titania is negligible.

7a.honestRead: Large gap on paper, but read it against what the engine cannot see. Dwalin's hone counters do get credited (counter growth is modeled), yet the equipment shell around him -- attaching, re-attaching, and stacking modifiers on one protected body -- is not: equipment reads as an ordinary permanent. Atsushi is a self-contained value creature that needs no such support, which is exactly the kind of card this model flatters. Keep Dwalin unless you want a genuinely different, gear-light deck.

7b.honestRead: Kemba's whole plan is making a cat token for every equipment she carries, and the model treats tokens as extra power on their maker rather than separate bodies -- so a wide board that blocks, trades, and carries its own gear collapses into one number. Second of sixteen despite that handicap is a strong showing. Keep Kemba; the +6.6 gap is an artifact of how tokens are counted, not a real deficit.

7c.honestRead: Bruse Tarl grants double strike and lifelink to a single attacker, and double strike has no representation in this engine at all -- the connect-rate model knows flying, menace, and trample, and nothing else. His signature turn is therefore worth zero here. Krenko's measured edge is real for a model that only counts bodies and power; against a live table Bruse Tarl's damage doubling is the bigger effect. Keep him.

7d.altCommander: Etali, Primal Conqueror // Etali, Primal Sickness
7d.honestRead: Stonebrow tops his own field, and unusually the number can be trusted: his payoff is trample damage on a big board, and trample is one of the few combat keywords this engine actually models (an elevated connect rate). Etali finishing 0.7 behind is inside noise. Keep Stonebrow -- this is the one deck-7 commander whose score is measuring roughly the right thing.

7e.honestRead: No alternative already in this deck beats Shadrix Silverquill by more than the seed-to-seed noise (-11.25 against 0.17), so the commander in the box is the right one on this evidence. The field is only the 3 legends already inside the deck whose color identity covers every card in it, not every legal commander in the colors.

8a.honestRead: Only two commanders in this field resolved a legal deck, so 'rank 2 of 2' is a thin result, not a verdict. Balin's refill-on-Dwarf-entry is partly credited (the engine does model card draw), but the burn half that comes online at Storied depends on counting discarded cards, which it does not track. Treat +1.3 as noise and keep Balin.

8b.honestRead: Depala pumps Dwarves and Vehicles and tutors off her own activation, and Vehicles are not modeled at all -- crew is not a mechanic this engine implements, so a meaningful slice of her deck reads as inert artifacts. Her tutor is also flattened into 'draw the best of three random cards.' The +16.4 gap is the largest in this deck and almost entirely an artifact. Keep Depala unless you drop the Vehicle package.

8c.honestRead: This is the most trustworthy comparison in deck 8: Grumgully's payoff is +1/+1 counters on non-Human creatures entering, and counter growth is modeled directly. Umaro measuring +5.2 ahead over a three-commander field is a real, if narrow, signal. Worth considering the swap on numbers alone -- though the field here was small enough that the result deserves a second look before acting on it.

8d.honestRead: Torbran adds two damage to every red source, and this engine has no per-source damage amplification -- damage is aggregated, never multiplied by a static effect. His single most important line is therefore worth nothing here, over a field of only two resolved commanders. Ignore the +2.9 and keep Torbran; the model is not measuring the card.

8e.honestRead: Feldon wins his field outright, and his reanimation-as-a-hasty-token effect is at least partly visible to the model (a recurring body each turn). The field was small (two resolved commanders), so treat this as confirmation rather than proof. Keep Feldon.

9a.honestRead: Read the whole of deck 9 together: every spellslinger commander here lands in the bottom third of its field, which is a systematic artifact, not five independent findings. The engine has no stack and no cast-triggered abilities, so magecraft, prowess, and every 'whenever you cast an instant or sorcery' payoff -- the entire reason these commanders are in the deck -- contributes nothing. Shantotto's mana-scaled growth and refill are invisible. Keep her; the +11.2 gap measures the model's blind spot, not the deck.

9b.honestRead: Veyran's text does one thing: double every magecraft trigger. The engine models no cast triggers at all, so her ability is worth precisely zero here, which is why she sits 15th of 16. This is the clearest example in the whole lineup of a commander the simulation cannot evaluate. Disregard the +12 entirely and keep Veyran.

9c.honestRead: Melek casts the top of your library and copies your instants and sorceries, and spell copying has no representation in this engine -- a copied spell is simply not a thing the model can produce. His measured 70 reflects a 6-mana body with no text. Keep Melek; the +9.9 gap is not a real comparison.

9d.honestRead: Niv-Mizzet finishing dead last of sixteen is a red flag about the measurement, not the card: his draw-and-ping loop fires on every card drawn, and the engine tracks card draw as a resource without firing per-draw triggers. His triple-blue-triple-red cost is fully modeled as a cost, though, so he is charged for his mana requirement and credited none of its payoff. Keep him.

9e.honestRead: Kess lets you recast an instant or sorcery from the graveyard each turn -- graveyard recursion of noncreature spells is outside this model, which recurs bodies but not spells. Bottom of a sixteen-commander field with her defining ability unmodeled is the expected outcome. Talrand's drakes do get partial credit as extra power. Keep Kess.

10a.altCommander: Dion, Bahamut's Dominant // Bahamut, Warden of Light
10a.honestRead: The whole of deck 10 needs the same caveat: this engine has no mana-cost taxation model, so a stax commander's core text is invisible. Grand Arbiter Augustin IV discounts your spells and taxes everyone else's, and neither half exists here -- he measures as a 4-mana 2/3. That is the entire explanation for the +23.4 gap. Keep him; nothing about this number describes the deck you would actually play.

10b.altCommander: Dion, Bahamut's Dominant // Bahamut, Warden of Light
10b.honestRead: Derevi untaps and taps permanents at will and recurs herself around removal, and this model has no tap-down state for permanents at all -- a tapped opponent's board is not something it represents. Her measured 48.7 is essentially a 3-mana 2/3 with no abilities. The +33.7 gap is the largest in the lineup and is entirely a modeling artifact. Keep Derevi.

10c.honestRead: Zur tutors a cheap enchantment directly onto the battlefield every time he attacks, and this engine flattens all tutoring into 'draw the best of three at random' -- the precision that makes Zur a build-around is gone. The enchantment suite he fetches is likewise scored as generic permanents. Treat +22.7 as unmeasured rather than measured, and keep Zur.

10d.honestRead: Braids tops her own field, which is worth noting precisely because the rest of deck 10 measured so badly: her effect is a recurring forced sacrifice, and repeated resource denial is something the engine partly represents through opponent damage and board state. Visara trailing by 1.3 is inside noise over a seven-commander field. Keep Braids.

10e.honestRead: Sen Triplets locks one opponent out of their own hand and lets you cast from it -- taking and casting an opponent's cards is not a mechanic this engine implements in any form. Combined with the missing taxation model that flattens the rest of the deck, her 54.9 measures a 5-mana 3/3 artifact creature. Keep Sen Triplets; the +21.4 is meaningless here.
